en.title: Batman Villain Burgess Meredith Starred in a Twilight Zone Masterpiece
en.summary: A legendary Twilight Zone episode featuring a future Batman foe is remembered as one of its best. The iconic actor delivered a performance that still resonates today.
en.body:
Long before he donned the top hat and wielded an umbrella as Gotham's avian antagonist, **Burgess Meredith** delivered a career-defining performance in one of television's most enduring anthology series. The 1959 episode of **The Twilight Zone**, titled "Time Enough at Last," remains etched in the minds of fans as a pinnacle of Rod Serling's visionary storytelling. Meredith portrayed Henry Bemis, a timid bank teller with a passion for reading, whose greatest wish – endless time to indulge his literary pursuits – is granted in the most ironic and devastating way imaginable.

The episode masterfully crafts a sense of profound isolation and tragic fate. Bemis, constantly interrupted by his wife and boss, finds solace only in books. After surviving a cataclysmic event that he believes has wiped out humanity, he discovers himself alone in a desolate world, surrounded by the remnants of libraries. His joy at finally having all the time in the world to read is shattered when his glasses break, rendering him unable to see the words he cherishes so deeply. It’s a gut-wrenching conclusion that perfectly embodies the show's signature blend of speculative fiction and existential dread.

## A Tale of Irony and Isolation

"Time Enough at Last" is frequently cited among **The Twilight Zone's** greatest episodes, a testament to its powerful narrative and Meredith's nuanced portrayal. The episode's impact is so significant that it has been referenced and parodied countless times, solidifying its place in pop culture history. Meredith's ability to convey both the meekness of Bemis and the sheer despair of his final moments is *remarkable*, making the viewer feel every ounce of his crushing disappointment. This episode stands as a prime example of how **The Twilight Zone** could explore complex human emotions through seemingly simple, yet profound, science fiction premises.

## Connecting Worlds: From Serling to Gotham

The legacy of "Time Enough at Last" is amplified by the knowledge that its star would later become a beloved villain in another iconic franchise. **Burgess Meredith's** subsequent role as the **Penguin** in the 1960s **Batman** television series cemented his status as a versatile and unforgettable performer. It’s a fascinating bit of trivia for fans who appreciate how actors can bridge different worlds and leave indelible marks on various genres. This connection highlights the rich tapestry of talent that passed through **The Twilight Zone**, including other notable actors like **Robert Duvall** and **William Shatner**, whose early appearances foreshadowed their future stardom.

## What's Next

While "Time Enough at Last" is a self-contained classic, the enduring appeal of **The Twilight Zone** continues to inspire new generations through its original run and subsequent revivals. Fans looking for more thought-provoking speculative fiction might explore recent seasons of **The Twilight Zone** on Paramount+ or revisit other standout episodes like "The Monsters Are Due On Maple Street." The impact of these timeless stories proves that great science fiction, much like a good book, never truly goes out of style.
